episode_title: Lessons from 40 Years in Law: Trial Preparedness, Client Trust, and Firm Growth

real_qa.q: What are the key lessons Don Macari learned from over 200 jury trials in his 41-year legal career?
real_qa.r: The biggest lesson is that trial work requires thorough preparation: you must know every fact, understand the rules of evidence, and build trust and rapport with the jury from the moment you enter the courtroom. Additionally, no trial ever goes exactly as planned, so lawyers must be ready to handle unexpected situations without showing stress. Trial work appears sexy on TV but in real life it demands intensive preparation, including many nights and weekends spent preparing openings and closings, and it is a stressful but rewarding profession.
real_qa.requete: lessons from 200 jury trials trial preparation

real_qa.q: How does the contributory negligence rule in North Carolina and Virginia compare to comparative negligence in other states?
real_qa.r: Contributory negligence in North Carolina, Virginia, and two other states bars recovery entirely if the plaintiff is found to have any negligence that contributes to the accident, whereas most states have comparative negligence where a plaintiff who is 20 percent at fault can still recover 80 percent of their damages. Macari described contributory negligence as a terribly harsh rule and stated that he and other trial lawyers associations try every year to get legislatures to change it because it is unfair and the first thing insurance adjusters use to argue against clients.
real_qa.requete: contributory negligence North Carolina Virginia bar recovery

real_qa.q: What is the true story behind A Few Good Men and Don Macari's first trial at Guantanamo Bay?
real_qa.r: Macari's first trial involved 10 Marines charged with attempted murder after performing a Code Red (blanket party) that injured Private Alvarado at Guantanamo Bay. The incident stemmed from Alvarado reporting a fence line shooting incident to NIS (now NCIS), leading his commanding officer to imply the Marines should punish him. Macari's client, David Cox, refused a plea deal because he claimed he was just following orders. Seven other Marines took administrative discharges, but Cox and two others went to trial; Cox was found guilty of simple assault when the jury found there was an implied order. The case was adapted into a Broadway play by Aaron Sorkin and later became the 1992 film A Few Good Men directed by Rob Reiner, starring Tom Cruise, Jack Nicholson, Demi Moore, and Kiefer Sutherland.
real_qa.requete: A Few Good Men Don Macari Guantanamo Bay Marines trial

real_qa.q: What advice does Don Macari give to young attorneys starting their own law firms?
real_qa.r: Macari advises young lawyers to find an area of law they are passionate about because legal practice is not a nine-to-five job and will consume much of their time. Most importantly, attorneys must treat law as both a profession and an honor profession, but also as a business by implementing proper management structures including a CFO, director of IT, director of advertising, and human resources director. He also emphasizes that while marketing is crucial to acquiring clients, the best advertising is word of mouth, and once clients are retained, delivering excellent service and maintaining good processes ensures reputation and sustainable business growth.
real_qa.requete: starting law firm advice young attorneys business management

real_qa.q: Why does Don Macari emphasize personal connection and body language in client relationships despite advances in AI and technology?
real_qa.r: Macari warns that while AI is wonderful and will change the law profession, lawyers must still be able to personally connect with clients by listening, watching body language, and understanding where clients are coming from, as people come to lawyers with problems they need advice on. He expressed concern that the younger generation, relying heavily on phones and technology, risks losing the communication skills necessary to read clients and build the trust required in legal relationships. He emphasized that you cannot convince a jury or client of something they do not believe in, and that trust and rapport start the moment you enter the courtroom or meet a client.
real_qa.requete: client trust body language communication lawyers AI technology

guest.bio_context: Don Macari has been practicing law for 41 years, starting with four years in the Navy JAG Corps handling mostly criminal work on a mobile trial team that tried cases on aircraft carriers and at Guantanamo Bay. In 2000, he co-founded his personal injury firm with 12 other people, growing it from 13 to over 100 people with offices across Tidewater, Raleigh, Fayetteville, and Charlotte, North Carolina. He has handled over 200 jury trials and specializes in personal injury, veterans practice, and Camp Lejeune cases. His first trial—an attempted murder case at Guantanamo Bay—inspired the 1992 film A Few Good Men.
